newsitem.title: USA: Conn gov picks new treasurer, but only for interim.
newsitem.headline: Conn gov picks new treasurer, but only for interim.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. George Rowland on Friday selected the deputy treasurer to complete the term of Treasurer Christopher Burnham who is resigning.
But Rowland made it clear the new appointee, Paul Silvester, will not serve beyond Burham's term, saying Silvester will not run in 1998 as a candidate for the office.
Silvester's appointment will be effective as soon as Burnham resigns, Rowland said, without elaborating further.

The present Treasurer said in late June he would resign to take a job with a Stamford investment firm that the Hartford Courant has said held a state contract during his tenure, but did not disclose the date he would leave.

The Republican governor, in prepared remarks, said "(Silvestor) has served as Chris Burnham's top deputy, is completely familiar with the day-to-day operations of the office, understands the complexities of managing the state's investments, and his appointment will provide a sense of continuity to the investment world."

The governor told the Hartford Courant he had received eight to nine applications for the position. The applications, which all were from Republicans, included Silvestor, Senator Win Smith of Milford, former Treasurer Joan Kemler, and Darien resident Steven Hart, who works with Burnham as chairman of the state's Investment Advisory Council, the paper said.
